claim_candidates.text: Silver Bullet qualifies as a canonical APO: it ships as host-integrated packaging (plugins/skill-source mirror, hooks, skills) for Claude/Codex/Cursor, persists cross-session state via .planning/ and runbooks, enforces deterministic quality gates (hooks/audits/release policy), routes to specialist subagents (gpt-5.6-sol-high policy, review ladders), positions as compliance wrapper above host runtimes, and claims release/governance enforcement (CI green mandatory, pre-release gate).

The APO market is thinly populated by self-labeled vendors; only Silver Bullet, AI-DLC, Conductor, and cc10x reliably evidence host-integrated process-layer packaging plus deterministic gates plus cross-session state. Most adjacent 'agentic workflow' tools collapse into single-SDLC-step or generic-agent-framework exclusion classes.

SDLC-plugin secondary market (Zuvo, GSD, Superpowers, BMAD-METHOD, GitHub Spec Kit, SuperClaude, Ruflo/Claude Flow, Oh My Pi) is the formidable substitute pool: each ships as a methodology pack/plugin above a host runtime and can replicate APO-grade enforcement without the APO brand. Zuvo is OSS-licensed per pack note.

BMAD-METHOD is a methodology pack (breakthrough-method-for-agentic-driven-development) that supplies phased SDLC roles and templates; it is plugin/skill-hook packaged, deterministic-gated via its template contracts, and orchestrates specialist agents — passing ≥3 inclusion criteria, so it must appear in solution cards even though it does not self-label APO.

GSD (Get Shit Done), Superpowers, GitHub Spec Kit, SuperClaude, Ruflo/Claude Flow, and Oh My Pi each evidence host-integrated packaging and at least one of {deterministic gates, cross-session state, specialist agents}; they belong in the secondary market chart and matrix, not in adjacent-only.

Factory / Factory.ai, Devin, Augment Cosmos, and Tembo are tertiary-market analyst-grade APO peers per the multi-market contract: they orchestrate multi-phase delivery, integrate host-style runtimes, and provide deterministic review/release artifacts, even though vendors do not self-label APO. Apply factory↔factory-ai dedupe alias.

Tembo, Magic.dev, and Cognition Scout round out the tertiary SaaS market as multi-phase autonomous-delivery peers; Cursor Background Agents, Sweep, Windsurf, Amazon Q, Sourcegraph Cody, Poolside, CodeRabbit, OpenHands, Cline, Continue, Aider, SWE-agent, and Open Interpreter are hard-excluded as single-SDLC-step tools or coding-agent runtimes.

Adjacent-only band (LangGraph, CrewAI, MetaGPT, LangChain, AxonFlow, Cavekit v4) is excluded from Top-N/MQ/Wave/matrix per pack: they are generic agent frameworks without a shipped, enforced SDLC process product.

Sunset list (GitHub Copilot Workspace, AutoGen, AgentGPT, Devika) is never plotted; AI-DLC and Conductor carry the heaviest public-claim weight for SDLC/DevOps-cycle enforcement alongside Silver Bullet.

Inclusion-criterion tally per market: APO core seeds pass 4–7 of 7 criteria; secondary plugin seeds pass 3–5; tertiary SaaS seeds pass 3–6. Core count of 8–24 in-scope solutions is achievable across all three markets without violating hard-exclusion lists.

claim_candidates.text: Silver Bullet is the deepest APO by process-lattice span: 85+ canonical skills, deterministic hooks, cross-session agentmemory, specialist subagent routing, and plugin/skill/hook packaging across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor — covering all 7 inclusion criteria versus 4-5 for nearest peers.

No APO competitor matches Silver Bullet's plugin-host triad (Claude Code + Codex + Cursor). Most APOs (Conductor, cc10x, Director, AgentHub, ATeam) target a single host — typically Claude Code only — making SB the only cross-host process orchestration layer in the primary market.

SDLC plugin secondary market (BMAD, GSD, Superpowers, GitHub Spec Kit, Oh My plugins, Zuvo/OSS, SuperClaude, Ruflo) represents the most credible APO substitution threat: each enforces a partial lifecycle span with methodology-specific gates, but none provides cross-session persistent state, deterministic hook enforcement, or specialist agent orchestration within a single package.

Zuvo's OSS license (not commercial) places it in the secondary plugin market rather than tertiary SaaS, but its workflow-orchestration surface makes it the most APO-adjacent secondary entry — closer to APO than GSD or BMAD in lifecycle span.

Tertiary agentic SDLC SaaS (Factory/Factory.ai, Devin, Augment Cosmos, Tembo) satisfies ≥5 inclusion criteria despite not self-labeling APO: multi-phase lifecycle, specialist agent routing (Devin's planner/coder/reviewer/architect roles), deterministic pass/fail gates, and quality/release enforcement claims. They are genuine APO peers per market definition, not adjacent tools.

AI-DLC (IBM) is the weakest APO core seed by enforcement depth: it defines a conceptual lifecycle for methodology guidance without shipping deterministic gates, cross-session state, or host-integrated plugin packaging. It belongs in the APO market per inclusion criteria §lifecycle_span alone but ranks below all shipped products.

cc10x and Conductor form a mid-tier APO cluster sharing complementary strengths: Conductor has stronger workflow orchestration UI and cross-session state; cc10x has deeper Claude Code hook integration, deterministic gates, and release enforcement. Neither matches SB's specialist agent routing or cross-host coverage.

The APO market has ~19 in-scope solutions (primary + secondary + tertiary), within the 8-24 core-count bound. Hard exclusions (Cursor Background Agents, Windsurf, Aider, Cline, OpenHands, CodeRabbit, etc.) are correctly excluded as single-step tools, coding agents, or host runtimes — not process orchestrators.

No APO product except Silver Bullet provides verifiable cross-session memory persistence (agentmemory, FTS5 knowledge base, observation audit trail) as a process-orchestration primitive. Conductor and Cavekit v3.1 claim workflow state only; Factory and Devin retain session context within a single cloud workspace but do not surface it as a reusable gate-check artifact.

Startup-weighted comparison matrix should weight cross-host coverage (SB), lifecycle span depth (SB, Devin, Factory), deterministic gate enforcement (SB, cc10x, Devin), and plugin-ecosystem size (SB, Oh My plugins) as the top differentiators — with SB leading on 3 of 4 and Devin leading on lifecycle span.
